judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard confidentiality legend; the only defect is the OCR-level misrendering 'THE MORTGAGE FUND LEC', which does not change meaning, and 'any reproduction' follows a comma splice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably beside the fuller confidentiality/trade-secret legend at c011, which permits disclosure to the recipient's own advisors; the two are cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate non-reliance and regulatory disclaimer with no term whose boundary is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c006 (no legal/tax advice) and c184 (access to information); nothing in the instrument grants the reliance this disclaims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recites the securities-law status of the Notes in definite terms; no ambiguous operative word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Investment Company Act', but c170 separately defines the same statute as the 'Company Act', a duplicate defined term for one statute across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Transfer restriction is stated absolutely ('may not be sold, transferred, assigned or hypothecated ... except as provided in the Note Purchase Agreement'), which is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c107 permits transfers 'to family trusts, to wholly-owned affiliates or by operation of law' without the Manager's consent, an exception this legend does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to prior sale' and an unqualified right to reject any subscription are conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c183 (accept or reject in sole and absolute discretion) and c088; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclaimer of advice with no operative obligation to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by c057 (lack of independent legal representation) and c118 (Company Counsel does not represent investors).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best judgment', 'material' variations and 'without unreasonable effort or expense' are soft, but the paragraph is a disclaimer rather than a promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disclaims projections while c012 states a target of 'approximately 8.00% or more per year' and c022 recites past returns, a mild recital-versus-disclaimer tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a comma splice ('THE COMPANY BELIEVES ... IS ACCURATE ..., THE COMPANY CANNOT GUARANTEE'), and OCR page furniture is embedded, but meaning survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the general disclaimers at c007 and c026; no other clause warrants third-party data.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Qualified in its entirety by reference to' the Offering Documents plus a reserved right to 'modify any of the terms' is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It competes with c185 (qualified in its entirety by the Note Purchase Agreement) and with c114, which requires Majority in Interest approval for modifications of Noteholder Agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; 'before a closing' is definite given the closing mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits c099's closing schedule and c005's right to reject subscriptions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trade-secret characterisation is asserted broadly ('its contents') and the carve-out for advisors is conditional, but the terms are workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps c001, which prohibits disclosure without consent full stop while this clause permits advisor disclosure; the overlap is cumulative but not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Superior returns with a conservative risk profile' and 'targeting to return approximately 8.00% or more' are promotional and vague, and 'the Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company' is stated flatly without qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That flat security promise sits against c019 and c108 (borrowings may be senior to the Noteholders' lien) and c164 (no assurance the security interest will be perfected or senior) — the classic recital-versus-operative conflict in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercial real estate or for other real estate related purposes' is a general catch-all sitting against the enumerated ownership/entitlement/development/rehabilitation list, leaving its reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c060 permits residential construction loans and loans collateralised by other loans, which reads more broadly than this stated purpose of financing 'commercial real estate'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Biographical and structural description; '81 years of experience ... among them' is odd but not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Manager 'expects to hire Bar-K', while c031 says the Manager 'has selected Bar-K' and c085 makes Bar-K the initial Servicer — a small inconsistency of tense and commitment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wording is definite; the quotation marks around '"loaning"' hint at characterisation but the mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its dates conflict with c099: initial closing 'on or before December 3, 2007' versus 'December 1, 2007', and monthly closings 'through May 1, 2009' versus a final closing by the sixth full quarter (estimated June 30, 2009).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to a minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized' is genuinely ambiguous — an average over what period, and averaged across what — and 'payment of principal will be deferred, at the discretion of the Company' cuts against a fixed maturity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c089 states the floor differently ('the Floating Rate will not be less than 8% on an annualized basis for a calendar year'), so the two operative statements of the same rate floor do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Very limited circumstances' for transferability is vague, though the prepayment mechanics are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c094 adds conditions this summary omits (60 days' notice, effective on the last business day of a fiscal quarter), and c107 names the permitted transfer categories.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Secured creditors of the Company' is a legal characterisation stated without qualification; the words themselves are otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c108 permits a senior secured Company Borrowing over the same Collateral and c164 warns the security interest may not be perfected or senior, so the unqualified 'secured creditors' statement is hard to reconcile with the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Raising Note proceeds to pay expenses and compensation is stated plainly, though 'other Company related expenses' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It authorises borrowings 'senior to the lien securing the Notes', which is in direct tension with c012 and c018's promise that Noteholders are secured by the Company's assets.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conservatively underwritten', 'quality real estate' and 'sub-prime mortgage market' are vague standards a court could be asked to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c066 expressly contemplates lending to borrowers already in default or lacking income sufficient to qualify at a bank, which is difficult to reconcile with the promise not to operate in the sub-prime market, and c079 contemplates occasional loan sales against 'will not source loans for the purpose of resale'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences of market commentary; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision depends on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proven lending record', 'well-diversified' and 'solid returns' are promotional adjectives, but the concrete claim ('no investor has experienced a loss of investment principal') is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The track-record claim runs against the illustration-only disclaimer at c026 and the 'no operating history' factor at c161.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numerical description of R.E. Loans' portfolio; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c055 describes the same affiliate with slightly different framing (ownership by B-4 Partners), but no operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Historical description with figures; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c028 and c029's account of B-4 Partners' predecessor partnerships.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '100% collection record' is an absolute claim whose scope ('loans it administers') is loose but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by the all-caps disclaimer immediately following at c026 and by c161's 'no operating history', a recital-versus-disclaimer tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long disclaimer in definite terms; embedded OCR page furniture does not alter meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the counterweight to the promotional recitals at c012, c022 and c025 and directs readers to the Risk Factors, which it correctly identifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive account of who manages what; no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c084 (Manager's responsibility) and c031/c032 (Servicer's role).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Biographical and affiliation description; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with c055's description of B-4 Partners and R.E. Loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Biography with figures; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict with c033 (Walter Ng as Servicer chairman).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Biography; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive; the statement that Bar-K is 'a real estate broker licensed by the California Department of Corporations' misdescribes the licensing agency but is not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Manager 'has selected' Bar-K while c014 says it 'expects to hire' Bar-K and c085 makes the Servicer role delegable to 'one or more qualified servicing entities'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Servicer will originate or arrange all loans acquired by the Company' is absolute; 'originate or arrange' is broad but the absolute 'all' is the exposed word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c074 says the Company will buy or originate 'most or all' of its loans through the Servicer and may purchase from unrelated third parties, and c050 lets the Manager retain other firms 'in lieu of the Servicer' — a direct conflict with 'all'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A name and title; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c029.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Biography; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c031's ownership description of Bar-K.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single cross-referencing line; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c030.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminate all or any portion of their business relationship ... at any time' is unusually one-sided and 'any portion' is undefined, giving a court something to bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 forbids the Manager to 'withdraw as the sole manager of the Company' without approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders, which this at-will termination right would nullify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The routing of compensation depending on whether the Company or the Manager contracts with the Servicer is convoluted but internally traceable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same mechanic is restated at c102's final sentence in compatible terms; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee formula is precise (1% per annum, 0.0833% monthly in advance), though the provision as extracted carries stray column headings from the table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim at c100 in the Summary of Principal Terms with the same numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payable only from Portfolio Loan interest that is received by the Company' is a clear condition; the table fragments make the entry hard to read but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c102 restates the Loan Service Fee as '0.0833%' monthly where this entry says '1/12 of 1% per month' — the same figure differently expressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '10% of late charges on delinquent Portfolio Loan payments received by the Company' is definite, though 'received by the Company' could attach to charges or payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c102 restates it as 'ten percent (10%) of late charges on delinquent payments' without the 'received by the Company' qualifier.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent it exceeds the regular stated interest rate payable to the Company' is a workable measure, though 'default interest' is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated in identical substance at c102; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anticipated to average between three percent (3%) and six percent (6%)' states an expectation rather than a cap, leaving the actual entitlement unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c050 confirms the fees 'may be higher or lower depending upon market conditions', which is consistent but underlines that no operative ceiling exists anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anticipated to average approximately $1,000 per loan' plus 'these fees may vary' sets no enforceable limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c102 gives the same item as 'approximately $1,000-$2,000 per Portfolio Loan', a direct numerical inconsistency between the table and the Summary of Principal Terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other than those borne by the Company or Servicer' defines the Manager's burden only by exclusion, which is circular with the companion definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c045 and c046 supply the excluded categories, and c101 adds a cap on Company organisational costs absent here, so the three definitions only work read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of Company Expenses (organisational fees, taxes, accounting, audit, investor communications, allocable rent) is closed and 'allocable rent' is vague as to allocation method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c101 states the same definition but caps organisational fees at 'a maximum of $500,000 or 1% of aggregate Principal ... whichever amount is greater'; this version has no cap at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence allocating Loan Service Expenses to the Servicer; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated at c103 in identical terms and dovetails with c044.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The footnote is cut off mid-sentence ('amounts generally charged for similar loans in the private'), and even completed it fixes the fee ceiling by the wholly undefined benchmark of 'amounts generally charged'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only ceiling on the servicing fee set at c039/c102, so its truncation matters to those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It asserts the Manager owes 'no direct fiduciary obligation to the Noteholders' while acknowledging fiduciary duty to members, and 'good faith and integrity' is a soft standard investors are told to rely on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indemnity standard here ('unless ... fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct') differs from c115's standard ('willful misconduct or gross negligence'), so the instrument states two different exculpation thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'These conflicts of interest are unlikely to be resolved' and 'except as may arise in the normal course of the relationship' are loose qualifiers on an otherwise descriptive passage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to a section called 'Fiduciary Responsibility of the Managing Member', which does not exist anywhere in the instrument (the heading at c048 is 'No Fiduciary Responsibility of Manager to Noteholders').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company will generally charge Portfolio Borrowers interest at the rate generally prevailing ... for loans to comparable borrowers of similar size, duration and security' is a doubly hedged and undefined benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence lets the Manager retain other firms 'in lieu of the Servicer', which conflicts with c032's statement that the Servicer will originate or arrange all Company loans.
